name: Warden · SAT Digital
oneLiner: Khmer-first moderation support for Telegram community operators, with enforcement decisions kept reviewable by humans.
question: Can Khmer community operators get useful moderation signals without handing enforcement authority to a model?
problem: Khmer community operators often moderate high-volume Telegram channels with little language-specific tooling and no visibility into why a model flagged a message. Silent automated enforcement in a low-resource language is a recipe for unfair, unexplainable moderation.
targetUsers: Operators of Khmer-language Telegram communities who need help spotting suspicious links and harmful content while keeping enforcement decisions — and their consequences — human.
whyItMatters: Moderation is governance in miniature: classification confidence, policy, and enforcement are three different things, and collapsing them harms real communities. False positives in a low-resource language fall hardest on the people with the least recourse.
exactRole: Model design and evaluation contribution within the SAT Digital product track.
teamContributions: SAT Digital is a CHNAI LAB product track with its own team; my contribution is scoped to model design and evaluation. [OWNER_INPUT_REQUIRED: Name the SAT Digital teammates and their roles]
research: Studying why English moderation benchmarks do not transfer to Khmer, and what explanation formats let a non-technical operator meaningfully review a flag instead of rubber-stamping it.
validation: Prototype-stage only. No public accuracy benchmark is claimed, and none should be trusted until a consented Khmer evaluation set exists — building that set is the next validation step.
proposedSolution: A moderation support tool that prioritizes explanations and review queues over silent automatic enforcement: the model advises, deterministic policy decides what is even eligible for action, and operators approve anything consequential, with an audit history behind it.
userWorkflow: Flags arrive in a review queue with explanations, not verdicts
The operator approves, rejects, or escalates each consequential action
Audit history records who decided what, and why
systemArchitecture: Advise → enforce → approve boundaries: model confidence is kept separate from policy decisions, which are kept separate from human approval. Audit history is a first-class component, not a log file.
methods: Khmer-specific evaluation instead of assuming English benchmark transfer, explanation-first classification output, and per-category false-positive measurement as the primary quality signal for moderation.
businessValue: Community trust is the product: operators who can explain their moderation decisions keep healthier communities. Commercial framing beyond that waits for the tool to exist publicly.
contractsPolicy: Moderation tooling sits directly on platform terms-of-service and content-policy questions: what the tool may scan, what it may store, and what enforcement it may recommend are policy decisions that precede code.
dataPrivacy: Community messages are sensitive. Evaluation data must be consented, message retention minimized, and audit records designed so accountability does not become surveillance.
risks: False positives can harm communities — which is why human review is a design requirement, not a feature
Policy and language coverage claims would be premature before operator testing
A moderation tool misused becomes a censorship tool; scope and audit design are the safeguards
humanApprovalPoints: Every consequential moderation action goes through operator approval
Any change to what content categories the tool acts on
Any collection of community messages for evaluation
technicalDecisions: Explanations and review queues prioritized over silent automatic enforcement
Khmer examples evaluated separately instead of assuming English benchmark performance transfers
Model confidence separated from policy decisions
Audit history kept for consequential moderation actions

completedWork.text: Model design and evaluation approach for Khmer-first classification

evidence.text: SAT Digital is publicly named as a CHNAI LAB product track (cyber-security tooling for Telegram).
Warden itself has no public repository, demo, or listing yet; the prototype and my contribution are stated by me.
Implementation details are private to the SAT Digital team.

results.text: No public accuracy benchmark exists, deliberately: publishing numbers before a consented Khmer evaluation set exists would be the exact failure mode this project is designed to avoid.

constraints: The system is a prototype with no public artifact to inspect
Khmer evaluation data must be consented before quality can be measured honestly
tradeoffs: Human review of every consequential action trades moderation speed for fairness — chosen knowingly
Keeping the work private until it is testable trades visibility for claim discipline

lessonsLearned: Moderation quality is measured in false positives per category, not aggregate accuracy
Separating confidence, policy, and enforcement is an architecture decision with ethical consequences
Low-resource language work forces honesty: without benchmarks to borrow, every claim needs its own evidence
nextValidation: Create a consented Khmer evaluation set
Measure false positives by content category
Test reviewer explanations and appeal handling with real operators
